title: TraceBridge: failure provenance lens and lightweight taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a compact, developer-friendly dashboard (TraceBridge lens) that surfaces end-to-end failure provenance for inference requests and a small, actionable taxonomy for operational teams. The goal is to make it fast to pivot from a top-level SLO breach to the causal domain (network / proxy / runtime / model / client) and recommend the next triage step. This work complements existing error dashboards by focusing on provenance chaining across RPC, gateway, serving runtime, and model evaluation boundaries.
background: Current dashboards aggregate errors by surface (timeout, 5xx, gRPC code) but do not present chained causality across hops or emphasize probable root cause candidates. On several recent incidents, oncall had to correlate traces, KV cache metrics, and model-side rejection events manually. We need a lightweight lens that stitches tracehook spans, gateway logs, runtime exit reasons, and model error signals into a single ranked view with suggested triage actions.
scope: IN: trace span aggregation for request flow (client -> gateway -> router -> runtime -> model), runtime exit_reason tagging, failure provenance ranking, Grafana/Console lens, alertable derived metrics. OUT: automated remediation, full incident response runbooks, heavy ML classification models for root-cause (we will use rule-based heuristics).
deliverables: TraceBridge dashboard in Console (interactive flow with span links)
Lightweight failure taxonomy and mapping doc (timeouts, overload, model-rejection, KV-cache-miss, auth/permission, network)
Derived metrics and SLIs (probable_root_domain, end_to_end_failure_rate, downstream_timeout_rate)
Tracehook enrichment rules and runtime exit_reason schema changes
Alert rules and SLO playbook snippets for common provenance outcomes
acceptance_criteria: TraceBridge displays the full request flow for a sampled set of requests with clickable spans into Trace Explorer
For >90% of SLO breach examples from last quarter, TraceBridge surfaces the correct probable domain (network/gateway/runtime/model) in the top-2 ranked candidates
Derived metric probable_root_domain is computed and stored in metrics-store with <1m latency
Two alert rules added: high-end_to_end_failure_rate and rapid-increase-in-probable-runtime-overload, each with annotated playbook steps
Documentation published (internal: Confluence link) and brief training session completed with oncall roster
implementation_notes: Design heuristic: score each hop by signals (latency spike, error code, exit_reason, kv_cache_miss, model_rejection). Rank domains by weighted score; weights tuned from historical incidents. Use tracehook attribute 'rb.provenance' for intermediate annotations. Accept a 10% false-positive rate initially; iterate with ops feedback.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: backend metric derivation and tracehook enrichment (week 1-2). Stage 2: Console dashboard alpha behind feature flag; invite SRE/Platform SMEs (week 3). Stage 3: open beta to product engineers and oncall, iterate on weights (week 4). Stage 4: GA and alerting oncw default (week 6).
migration_notes: No data migration required. New derived metric names will be prefixed with 'tb_' to avoid collisions. Tracehook schema bump is additive; runtime SDK will add optional exit_reason tag. Consumers should fallback if tag missing.
open_questions: What sampling rate for traces will provide statistical confidence without excessive cost? (ops suggestion: start with 10% for error traces)
Do we need a privacy review for storing model rejection payloads in traces?
Should alerts route to runtime oncall or gateway oncall when probable_root_domain is ambiguous?
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on taxonomy clarity and triage actions. The taxonomy is intentionally small to avoid analysis paralysis. Please provide examples of recent incidents to validate ranking heuristics.
